filter: A line is drawn when opened <= year and (closed > year or the feature has no closed year). This extract has no closed years.
simplify: Douglas-Peucker at about 100 meters, then coordinates rounded to 4 decimal places. Gaps of 2 km or less between pieces of the same route were closed with a straight segment. Fragments shorter than 2 km that did not join were dropped.

features.name: Lexington & Ohio Railroad
features.summary: Kentucky's first railroad. Horse-drawn cars reached Frankfort from Lexington on 31 January 1834; the first steam run followed in January 1835. The line was chartered to carry Bluegrass goods toward the Ohio River.

features.name: Louisville & Frankfort Railroad
features.summary: Closed the gap from Frankfort to the Ohio River at Louisville, with through service in 1851 after the Kentucky River bridge was finished.

features.name: Louisville & Nashville main line
features.summary: Opened south from Louisville in stages from 1855, climbing Muldraugh's Hill to reach Elizabethtown in June 1858. Track met at Bowling Green on 10 August 1859, and the first through train to Nashville ran on 27 October 1859.

features.name: Cincinnati Southern Railway
features.summary: Built by the city of Cincinnati for a direct route to Southern markets that bypassed Louisville and the L&N. It was open to Somerset by 23 July 1877, crossing the Kentucky River on High Bridge, and through service to Chattanooga began in 1880.

features.name: Mountain Parkway
features.summary: Winchester to Campton opened 14 January 1963, and Campton to Salyersville was dedicated 1 November 1963. It was built to open up eastern Kentucky.

features.name: Western Kentucky Parkway
features.summary: Elizabethtown to near Eddyville opened in 1963, and the extension to I-24 at Eddyville followed in 1968.

features.name: Bluegrass Parkway
features.summary: Opened 27 October 1965 between Elizabethtown and the Bluegrass at Versailles.

features.name: Purchase Parkway
features.summary: Opened in 1966 (provisional) through the Jackson Purchase, from Calvert City to Fulton.

features.name: Pennyrile Parkway
features.summary: Opened in 1969 (provisional) between Henderson and Hopkinsville.

features.name: Audubon Parkway
features.summary: Opened 18 December 1970 between Henderson and Owensboro.

features.name: Daniel Boone (Hal Rogers) Parkway
features.summary: London to Hazard. Sources disagree on the opening year: 1971 or 1974.

features.name: Green River (Natcher) Parkway
features.summary: Opened in 1972 (provisional) between Bowling Green and Owensboro.

features.name: Cumberland (Louie B. Nunn) Parkway
features.summary: Opened in 1973 (provisional) from I-65 near Glasgow east to Somerset.

features.name: High Bridge
features.summary: High Bridge carried the Cincinnati Southern over the Kentucky River palisades; it was finished in February 1877.

counties.source: US Census Bureau 2023 Cartographic Boundary File, counties 1:500,000 (cb_2023_us_county_500k), public domain
counties.process: Filtered to STATEFP 21 (120 counties), mapshaper simplify 8% keep-shapes, interior lines only; labels are inner points.

sections.note: Each route split into opening sections. Every date is provisional; dateSourced:false marks sections whose opening year is not yet sourced. Frankfort-Louisville geometry is the modern USDOT/BTS NTAD rail line (public domain).

v2.eraColors: Line color steps by completion decade, light amber (1830s) to deep red-brown (1970s). Sections not yet open at the slider year are drawn faint and dashed.

sectionsSourced.note: Per-section sources are in sections.geojson (sources[]). dateStatus is sourced or disputed. Parkway years stay provisional. whyInferred marks notes that are our inference.
